root_cause.text: The driver manually freed a WoL IRQ using `free_irq()` that was allocated with `devm_request_irq()`, causing a double-free when the device resource manager automatically freed the same IRQ during device cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes calls to `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy()` function which explicitly called `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv)`. The commit message explicitly states "We do not need to free wol_irq since it was instantiated with devm_request_irq(). So devres will free for us." This indicates the IRQ was allocated with the devm (device-managed) API in the original code (commit a2f0751206b0), but the cleanup code was manually freeing it, resulting in a double-free vulnerability when the devm framework automatically freed the resource during device removal.

Author: Justin Chen <justin.chen@broadcom.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/asp2/bcmasp.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/asp2/bcmasp.c
index 834
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a double-free vulnerability in two functions: `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_shared()` and `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_per_intf()`. Both functions manually call `free_irq()` on IRQs that were allocated using `devm_request_irq()` in `bcmasp_get_and_request_irq()`. Specifically: (1) Line 465: `ret = devm_request_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, bcmasp_isr_wol, 0, pdev->name, priv);` allocates the IRQ with device-managed resource tracking. (2) Line 520: `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv);` in `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_shared()` manually frees the IRQ. (3) Line 533: `free_irq(intf->wol_irq, priv);` in `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_per_intf()` manually frees the IRQ. These manual `free_irq()` calls will cause a double-free when the device resource manager automatically frees the same IRQ during device cleanup. The fix would be to either use `request_irq()` instead of `devm_request_irq()`, or remove the manual `free_irq()` calls entirely and let the devm framework handle cleanup.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit REMOVES the vulnerable code rather than introducing or fixing it. The vulnerability root cause describes a double-free where `free_irq()` was manually called on an IRQ allocated with `devm_request_irq()`. In this commit, the per-interface WoL IRQ allocation code (`bcmasp_init_wol_per_intf` and `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy_per_intf`) is completely removed. The remaining `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy()` function still calls `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv)` at lines 1159-1160, but this is now only used for the shared WoL IRQ case (not per-interface). The commit consolidates to a single WoL IRQ model by removing asp-v2.0 support, which was the version with the problematic per-interface IRQ handling. Since the vulnerable construct (per-interface `free_irq()` on `devm_request_irq()` allocated IRQs) is being removed in this commit, this is a fix commit, not a bug-introducing commit.
